intended_object: An auxiliary construction used to prove the Fubini theorem for colimits. Given colimit cocones `D j` under each `curry.obj G j` and a cocone `c` under `G : J × K ⥤ C`, it builds a cocone with the same point `c.pt` over the diagram `j ↦ (D j).pt`. I inferred this from the docstring and from its use in `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Limits/Fubini.lean`.
explanation:
This is a helper construction for the proof that colimits over `J × K` can be computed one variable at a time (`colim_j colim_k = colim_{(j,k)}`). It is the dual of `coneOfConeUncurry`. It is not a named concept in the literature; it is the step "a cocone under `G` induces, by the universal property of each inner colimit, a cocone over the outer diagram".

The body does this correctly. Each leg is the map `(Q j).desc` out of the colimit `D j`, induced by the restricted cocone `k ↦ c.ι.app (j, k)`. Naturality in `j` is checked with `hom_ext`, i.e. by uniqueness of maps out of a colimit.

Since it is an implementation device for the Fubini proof rather than a mathematical object in its own right, the verdict is `not_a_mathematical_object`.
